## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates real-world multi-tenant isolation, exactly-once guarantees, cross-region replication, and cost-aware retention using AWS DVA primitives. It tests the ability to blend data residency constraints with practical engineering tradeoffs.

## Key Concepts
- Tenant-scoped partitioning and sharding
- Idempotent processing and deduplication
- Cross-region replication and data residency
- Retention policies and lifecycle management
- OpenTelemetry integration and end-to-end tracing
- Cost controls and tenant-level observability

## Architecture Overview
The solution leverages Kinesis Data Streams for high-throughput ingestion, partitioned by composite keys (tenantId + region) to enable tenant-scoped sharding. Lambda or Fargate consumers implement idempotent processing using DynamoDB conditional writes with client-generated idempotency keys. S3 serves as the immutable event store with tenant-specific prefixes, enabling policy-based routing and per-tenant retention via Object Lifecycle rules. Cross-region replication is achieved through Kinesis Stream Fan-Out or DynamoDB Global Tables, with IAM cross-account roles enforcing data residency boundaries.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests multi-region data engineering, data quality, deduplication, anomaly detection, and tenant isolation under AWS DVA. It also probes error handling (DLQ) and testing strategy.

## Key Concepts
- IoT Core to Kinesis Streams integration for MQTT devices

## Code Example

-- Example KDA SQL: compute rolling mean per device
SELECT deviceId,
       AVG(metric) OVER (PARTITION BY deviceId ORDER BY ts ROWS BETWEEN 299 FOLLOWING AND CURRENT ROW) AS rolling_avg,
       CASE WHEN ABS(metric - rolling_avg) > threshold THEN 'ANOMALY' ELSE 'OK' END AS status
FROM input_stream
```

- What metrics and alarms would you place to monitor data quality, latency, and tenant budgets?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical knowledge of data masking, data residency, retention governance, and auditing in real-world AWS DVA pipelines. - Tenant-scoped masking policies and a centralized policy store (DynamoDB)
- Ingress processing with Lambda/Fargate per-tenant logic

- Audit visibility via Dead Letter Queue
- Replay semantics using raw data with idempotent re-ingest

function maskPII(record, policy) {

  if (policy.redact.includes('email')) record.email = 'REDACTED@domain.com';
  if (policy.redact.includes('phone')) record.phone = 'REDACTED';
  return record;
}
```

- What are the latency, storage, and cost trade-offs of maintaining raw + redacted copies and enabling replay?
